---
title: Installation and reproducibility
---

## Install the research library

Trex is distributed from [apoorvalal/trex](https://github.com/apoorvalal/trex). **Do not run `pip install trex`: that PyPI name is an unrelated project.** Python 3.10 or later is required.

Choose an environment with the appropriate [PyTorch build](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/) for your CPU or accelerator first. Then install this repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/apoorvalal/trex.git
cd trex
python -m pip install -e .
```

The editable installation is convenient when modifying methods or running the included notebooks. A non-editable installation needs no permanent checkout:

```bash
python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/apoorvalal/trex.git"
```

For a reproducible experiment, replace the moving branch with a full commit hash. For example, the correctness-update snapshot is:

```bash
python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/apoorvalal/trex.git@98df3cb7880df8c2b61ed0594c43c96e16bee93f"
```

This pins Trex, **not its dependencies**. Record the Python, Torch, CUDA/driver (if used), NumPy and SciPy versions too. Current version metadata remains `0.1.0`, so a Git revision identifies development snapshots more precisely than that version string.

## Runtime and optional dependencies

The core installation includes Torch, NumPy, SciPy, pandas and `pytorch-minimize`. Many methods use Torch throughout; GEL and score estimation also use CPU-side numerical routines. Installing Trex does not turn every routine into a GPU kernel.

```bash
# Independent estimator references and tests
python -m pip install -e '.[test]'

# Quarto execution and API documentation tools
python -m pip install -e '.[docs]'
```

The [Quarto CLI](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) is a separate installation. Large-model generation uses optional Transformers/PEFT/quantization tooling described in its [guide](../guides/llm-generators.qmd); those dependencies and model weights are not required for regression, choice or panel estimation.

## Verify the environment

```{python}
import platform
import torch
import trex

print({"python": platform.python_version(), "torch": torch.__version__,
       "trex": trex.__version__, "cuda_available": torch.cuda.is_available()})
```

The executable guides use `device="cpu"` deliberately, so they do not require a GPU. This does not imply CPU and CUDA are equally fast or bitwise identical. See [numerical conventions](numerics.qmd) before moving a workload between devices.
